product.ta-alphatronic-p30.summary: The P30 added a second processor to retain 8-bit programs and run 16-bit ones.
product.ta-alphatronic-p30.history: Triumph-Adler showed the P30 in Hanover in 1983. It was based on the P3, and the company offered to add the second processor to systems already installed. CP/M-86 was planned, and MS-DOS was in preparation.
product.ta-alphatronic-p30.technical.con: The add-on card expanded the software the machine could use. The P3’s 8085 handled the 8-bit environment and the card carried an Intel 8088 for the 16-bit environment.
product.ta-alphatronic-p30.technical.ver: BluMach has no runnable profile for this model.
product.ta-alphatronic-p30.technical.lim: Hash-checked MOS, keyboard firmware and the 8088 card ROM are preserved. MAME marks the P30 as not working and leaves card emulation for booting DOS pending.
